chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazi', from Ali ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him),
regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'O my regret, for what I wasted regarding the Side of Allah [39:56],'

He said: 'The Side of Allah is the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and similarly those who came after him from the successors in the exalted station, until the matter reaches the last of them.'

key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءُ: The successors/legatees — referring to the Imams of the Ahlulbayt who succeeded Imam Ali
key_terms.الْمَكَانُ الرَّفِيعُ: The exalted/high station — the elevated spiritual and religious position of the Imams
key_terms.جَنْبِ اللَّهِ: The 'Side of Allah' — a Quranic expression from 39:56, interpreted here as the divine authority and proximity embodied in the Imam

ai.seo_question: What does 'janb Allah' (Side of Allah) mean in Surah al-Zumar 39:56 according to Imam al-Kazim?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) interprets the Quranic phrase 'janb Allah' (the Side of Allah) in Surah al-Zumar (39:56) as referring esoterically to Imam Ali (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all the Imams who succeed him until the last one. This narration reflects the Shia hermeneutical tradition of applying the concept of divine proximity and authority ('janb') to the Ahlulbayt, presenting the Imams as the embodiment of nearness to God on earth. The audience, consisting of Imam al-Kazim's companions in 2nd-century AH Iraq, would have understood this as reinforcing the doctrine of Imamate — that the Imams occupy the highest spiritual station as the successors of the Prophet.
